root_cause.text: In btrfs snapshot creation, create_pending_snapshot() treated -EOVERFLOW from adding a BTRFS_UUID_KEY_RECEIVED_SUBVOL entry to the UUID tree as a fatal transaction error, even though repeated snapshots of the same received subvolume can legitimately overflow that leaf item and the entry is non-critical.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message says repeated snapshots “reach a BTRFS_UUID_KEY_RECEIVED_SUBVOL item overflow” and cause “Transaction aborted (error -75)”; the patch adds a special case in fs/btrfs/transaction.c to ignore `ret == -EOVERFLOW` after `btrfs_uuid_tree_add(..., BTRFS_UUID_KEY_RECEIVED_SUBVOL, ...)` with comments stating it is safe to ignore and avoids user-triggerable transaction aborts.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: In btrfs snapshot creation, create_pending_snapshot() treated -EOVERFLOW from adding a BTRFS_UUID_KEY_RECEIVED_SUBVOL entry to the UUID tree as a fatal transaction error, even though repeated snapshots of the same received subvolume can legitimately overflow that leaf item and the entry is non-critical.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The commit message says repeated snapshots “reach a BTRFS_UUID_KEY_RECEIVED_SUBVOL item overflow” and cause “Transaction aborted (error -75)”; the patch adds a special case in fs/btrfs/transaction.c to ignore `ret == -EOVERFLOW` after `btrfs_uuid_tree_add(..., BTRFS_UUID_KEY_RECEIVED_SUBVOL, ...)` with comments stating it is safe to ignore and avoids user-triggerable transaction aborts.

intent_record.intent_summary: Treat -EOVERFLOW from received UUID tree insertion as non-fatal during snapshot creation to avoid unnecessary transaction aborts when many snapshots share the same received root.
intent_record.what: The change adds a comment block and inserts a new conditional after the call to btrfs_uuid_tree_add() that converts a return value of -EOVERFLOW to 0 before the existing error check that aborts the transaction for unexpected errors other than -EEXIST.
intent_record.how: At runtime, if adding the received UUID subvolume entry to the UUID tree fails with -EOVERFLOW because the item has reached its leaf limit, snapshot creation will now continue successfully instead of treating it as a fatal error and aborting the transaction. This prevents transaction aborts during creation of many snapshots of the same received root while preserving acceptable behavior for deletion and send/receive paths described in the comment.

grouping_result.intent: Treat -EOVERFLOW from received UUID tree insertion as non-fatal during snapshot creation to avoid unnecessary transaction aborts when many snapshots share the same received root.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it makes -EOVERFLOW from inserting a received UUID entry into the UUID tree non-fatal during snapshot creation, preventing unnecessary transaction aborts for repeated snapshots of the same received subvolume.

candidates.rationale: This condition wrongly treated -EOVERFLOW from btrfs_uuid_tree_add() as a fatal error because it only exempted -EEXIST. The root cause is precisely the failure to also treat -EOVERFLOW as non-fatal for received UUID tree insertion during snapshot creation.
Once -EOVERFLOW reached this line through the overly broad error check, the transaction was unnecessarily aborted even though the UUID tree insertion was non-critical in this case.
This propagated the mistaken fatal handling path for -EOVERFLOW after UUID tree insertion, causing snapshot creation failure instead of continuing.

vuln_statements.explanation: This conditional is the root vulnerable statement because it classified every UUID tree insertion error other than -EEXIST as fatal, thereby incorrectly including -EOVERFLOW. That directly caused legitimate repeated received-subvolume snapshots to enter the fatal error path.

After the incorrect condition allowed -EOVERFLOW into the error path, this statement aborted the transaction even though the received UUID tree insertion failure was non-critical for snapshot creation.
This statement completed propagation of the mistaken fatal handling by forcing snapshot creation failure once -EOVERFLOW was misclassified as fatal.
